name: Vegetarian Enfrijoladas

ingredients.name: vegetable stock or reserved bean cooking liquid
vegetarian fresh crumbly cheese made with vegetarian coagulants

steps: Dice 80 g onion and the garlic; finely dice the remaining 60 g onion for garnish. Heat 10 ml oil in a saucepan and soften the first onion portion for 4 minutes. Add garlic and cumin for 30 seconds, then stir in the drained cooked black beans and vegetable stock. Simmer for 5 minutes.

Blend the bean mixture until completely smooth, then return it to the saucepan. Add the salt and simmer gently for 3–5 minutes until it forms a thick but pourable sauce; loosen with a splash of water if necessary. Keep warm over low heat. Check that the fresh cheese is made with vegetarian coagulants.

Brush a wide frying pan with the remaining 10 ml oil. Warm each corn tortilla for about 15–20 seconds per side so it becomes pliable without crisping. Keep the warmed tortillas under a clean cloth. Do not use them cold, as they may split when folded.

Using tongs, dip one warm tortilla at a time into the warm black-bean sauce to coat both sides. Transfer it to a plate, sprinkle a little of the cheese on one half and fold over. Repeat to make eight sauced, folded tortillas, arranging two on each serving plate. Spoon the remaining bean sauce over them.

Finish each plate with the finely diced raw onion, remaining crumbled vegetarian cheese, crema, coriander and avocado slices. Serve immediately while the tortillas are soft and the dark bean sauce is warm; the coating should be black-bean sauce, not tomato or chilli enchilada sauce.
tips: Blend beans until silky and keep the sauce loose enough to coat tortillas; a dry bean paste will tear them. The reviewed photo shows folded tortillas beneath glossy dark bean sauce with white cheese, onion, crema, coriander and avocado.
notes: Quantities serve four adults. Check the doneness cues in each step and adjust seasoning to taste. Jain suitability depends on your household ingredient rules.
